Subject: Generation hiccup — temporary timeouts on /v1/generate (Jan 19, 2027)

Hi Anita / SummitBridge ops team,

Quick advisory: between ~09:05–09:45 PST we observed elevated p95/p99 latency and intermittent timeouts for hosted generation endpoints (primarily /v1/generate and websocket-based chat streams) for customers in the us-west region. We put a temporary routing fallback in place at 09:18 which reduced tail latency for most traffic; a full mitigation rolled out by 09:44.

Impact summary:
- Scope: ~12% of requests experienced timeouts (HTTP 504) or >2s additional tail latency.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, chat streams (region: us-west).
- Time window: 09:05–09:44 PST (peak impact 09:10–09:25).

What we did:
- Switched affected traffic to the fallback model pool and enabled aggressive prefix caching for long-running sessions.
- Isolated a degraded kernel on a subset of GPU workers and kicked an automated replacement policy (workers drained and reprovisioned).
- Post-incident: ran KV-cache warmup and a targeted prefix-cache restore to prevent repeated cold starts.

Follow-ups:
- We will publish a short postmortem with timeline and root cause analysis here: https://redwood.app/postmortems/2027-01-19-generation-hiccup (draft in progress).
- Attachment: incident_summary_QA.pdf (quick Q&A + token impact estimate).

If you saw errors in any specific runs / job ids please send request ids or sample timestamps and we will run a targeted audit. Apologies for the disruption — we know this landed close to your morning ramp.

Thanks,

Hi Anita — thanks for the quick note.

Requested artifacts: attached a short log snippet (request_log_snippet.txt) with representative request ids and timestamps covering the peak window (09:10:12–09:25:43 PST). If you want a full export we can push it to a shared S3/Drive with an HB key — tell us the preferred location and we'll provision access.

Credits / SLA: our operations team will run a formal impact assessment as part of the postmortem; if the incident meets the SLA outage definition we will apply a prorated service credit per the terms in section 5.2 of the Master Services Agreement. Ben will coordinate a follow-up with procurement.

Dedicated capacity: Dedicated pools reduce surface area for noisy neighbor and kernel-level contention because you control the capacity commit and we avoid routing between multi-tenant pools. That said, the root cause here was a rare kernel degradation combined with a cold-cache amplification — a Dedicated pool would have reduced cross-tenant blast radius but would not have prevented a kernel-level bug on the worker itself. Our SREs will include recommendations for both shorter-term runtime hardening and longer-term dedicated/quantization guidance in the postmortem.

Post-incident next steps:
- Postmortem draft (link above) expected EOD today; final doc targeted by Jan 22.
- We will run a customer-only review (30m) to walk through timeline and remediation; Ben will propose slots.
- Attachment: incident_summary_QA.pdf (includes token impact estimate ~18M tokens, affected endpoints, and immediate mitigation steps).

Apologies again — appreciate your patience. We want to make sure operational continuity is tighter going forward.

Best,
